study: Three engines on the same inverse problem: bounded-terminal tree GP, PySR with numerically-optimised unbounded constants, and nested-template model selection in which every structure of interest is an explicit candidate. The question is whether the structures 10.43 failed to discover are missing from the representation, from the fitness, or from the data.

protocol.template_selection: BIC on fit rows, held-out RMSE, and held-out RMSE restricted to frames at >=90% of the observed speed support
protocol.shared_accuracy_metric: R^2 of the horizontal increment law on the shared held-out transition bank; gplearn scores its seed-bagged law, PySR its selected model, the template engine its tail-selected structure

rigid_bound.reading: The bound is recoverable: with the clamp as an explicit candidate the template engine returns 48.000 against a true 48.0, and BIC selects it in 100% of replicates. Free tree search finds it in 0% of replicates (gplearn) and 0% (PySR). PySR's constants are unbounded and numerically optimised, and on the shared eval bank it fits the horizontal increment law better than gplearn (0.988 vs 0.805) while missing the same structure, so neither the terminal range nor the accuracy of the fit explains the miss.  Its driven map stays within 0.213 px/frame of the observed velocity support without ever turning over inside it, so it has no fixed point and the probe registers no bound. What the three engines separate on is the criterion, not the repertoire: the constraint binds on 27.1% of held-out synthetic frames and on 0.0% of the telemetry test split, and an aggregate error metric prices it at essentially nothing on either - the template engine is the only one of the three that scores any structure on the binding frames separately.

gravity_gate.reading: The held-jump gate is a step in the velocity increment, so a tree without a conditional has to approximate a jump of -2.80 px/frame. Measured separations and recovery rates: gplearn separates by -1.35 and recovers the gate in 0.33 of replicates; pysr separates by -2.80 and recovers the gate in 1.00 of replicates; templates separates by -2.80 and recovers the gate in 1.00 of replicates.

real_telemetry.reading: On genuine telemetry: gplearn fits the horizontal law with held-out R^2 -0.000 and reports no bound; pysr fits the horizontal law with held-out R^2 0.430 and reports a bound at 34.193 (52.5% from the WRAM reference 72.0); templates fits the horizontal law with held-out R^2 0.989 and reports a bound at 47.775 (33.6% from the WRAM reference 72.0). Inside the template engine the BIC and tail criteria pick H6_contact and H5_coast, different structures, so the selection criterion still decides the reported law on real data even where every candidate carries the constraint.
